jobs.title: Continuous Improvement Quality Engineer (CIQE)
jobs.description:
Primary Function of the Position
Ensure that quality systems, products, and manufacturing processes comply with quality standards by supporting and driving improvements in the organization and in accordance with international industry practices and regulations (e.g., ISO 13485, 21CFR820).  Meet objectives, provide support and expertise in NC & corrective and preventive action (CAPA) process and system and implementing actions to drive the improvement. S/he will partner with subject matter experts on various NC/CAPA activities in addition to supporting other improvement initiatives.  S/he will evolve existing processes/systems to ensure timely escalation, identification, and robust investigation of product quality and compliance issues within a closed-loop quality management system.
Essential Job Duties
- Support and comply with Company and Site’s Health, Safety, and Environmental programs and requirements, including:

- - Use of personal protective equipment (PPE) as applicable.

- Use devices, accessories, tools, and equipment according to the process, verifying that they are in good condition for use and reporting those that are in poor condition for repair.

- Communicates unsafe acts or conditions to their superiors.

- Participates in the Health, Safety, and Environment courses established.

- Maintains order and cleanliness in the workstation (5S) under responsibility.

- Complies with health regulatory and International Standard (ISO13485) requirements, Company and site policies, operating procedures, processes, and task assignments.

- Participate in or lead completion of NC & CAPA projects, assuring compliance, quality, and timeliness of records.

- Communicate confidently and effectively with all levels of management, peers, and key stakeholders, including timely escalation of quality issues.

- Lead and collaborate with cross-functional teams using various methodologies (e.g., Six Sigma root cause analysis/problem-solving skills).

- Independently investigate, gather data, trends, and perform preliminary analysis.

- Process requests, ensuring subject matter experts and action item owners are assigned and provide timely responses in alignment with quality goals.

- Leads meetings and communications for NC/CAPA updates, information, and concerns.

- Responsible for assisting with metrics and reporting in accordance with established procedures.

- Support the team in delivering and overseeing the NC & CAPA training program.

- Assist in initiating, processing, and completing NC & CAPA records in the electronic system.

- Execute and provide on-time completion of Quality Engineering deliverables.

- Provide support and NC’s or CAPA’s process/system subject matter expertise during audits and inspections.

- Support the review and approval of any documentation required by NC/CAPA deliverables.

- Mentor CAPA teams and colleagues who are beginner-level in NC/CAPA processes and systems.
Required Skills and Experience
- Quality Engineer: Systems, Assurance, or Quality Control – Minimum 4 Years experience

- Have worked in a regulated manufacturing industry: Medical devices, Pharmaceuticals, Aerospace, Automobile, Food, etc. - Minimum 4 Years

- Previous NC & CAPA and/or engineering experience and demonstrated use of quality tools/methodologies. - Minimum 4 Years of work experience

- Detailed knowledge of Quality System Regulations (21CFR820) and ISO 13485. - Minimum 3 Years

- Ability to work in a highly matrixed and geographically diverse business environment

- Quality/Compliance focus and attention to detail

- Critical thinking skills for analyzing risk, use of root cause analysis tools, and technical aptitude to collect and analyze data for determining an improvement strategy

- Expertise in cGMP and NC/CAPA documentation

- Computer skills (advanced Microsoft Office Package and statistical/data analysis and report writing skills)

- Demonstrated impactful project management and leadership skills, including the ability to lead multi-departmental project teams and resolve quality-related issues in a timely and effective manner

- Ability to work within a team and as an individual contributor in a fast-paced, changing environment

- Ability to leverage and/or engage others to accomplish projects

- Strong verbal/written communication skills with ability to communicate effectively at multiple organizational levels

- Multi-tasks, prioritizes. and meets deadlines in a timely manner

- Strong interpersonal, organizational, and follow-up skills

- Passionate about making products and processes better

Required Education and Training
- Engineering Bachelor’s degree - Preferably in science or healthcare fields.

Working Conditions
- Desk and meeting rooms

Preferred Skills and Experience
- ASQ certification : CQE, CQA, Knowledge of Process improvement tools and methodologies (Lean, Six Sigma) is preferred.

- Green or Black Belt Certification in Lean or Six Sigma is a plus

- NC or CAPA Review and Approval Project Management experience

- Experience working in a broader enterprise/cross-division business unit model

jobs.title: Corporate Development Senior Manager
jobs.description:
Primary Function of Position
The individual in this role will manage Intuitive’s corporate development efforts for its da Vinci and Ion business units, including sourcing, investigating and negotiating a variety of transactions for the company.  Deal types will include strategic equity investments, strategic partnerships, co-marketing and co-development agreements, both in- and out-licensing, and M&A.
Essential Duties and Responsibilities
- Support corporate development activities for Intuitive's da Vinci and Ion business units, including the identification, evaluation, and execution of strategic partnerships, investments, licensing transactions, and M&A opportunities.
- Identify and assess external technologies, companies, and market opportunities aligned with Intuitive's strategic priorities and technology roadmap.
- Lead or support all phases of transactions, including sourcing, relationship development, business case creation, valuation, due diligence, structuring, negotiation, contracting, integration planning, and closing.
- Manage transaction workstreams and coordinate cross-functional teams to evaluate strategic, technical, commercial, financial, legal, and regulatory considerations.
- Develop strategic assessments, financial analyses, valuation models, and recommendations to support decision-making.
- Partner with business and technology leaders to understand priorities, capability gaps, and opportunities for external innovation.
- Collaborate with Corporate Development, Strategy, Finance, Legal, and Business Unit leaders to advance opportunities aligned with corporate objectives.
- Build and maintain relationships with external companies, investors, advisors, entrepreneurs, and strategic partners.
- Prepare transaction materials and recommendations for senior leadership and executive review.
- Support and, where appropriate, lead negotiations and transaction execution activities.
- Maintain ongoing partner relationships and support post-transaction governance and integration efforts.
- Provide regular updates on active opportunities, transactions, and external relationships to Corporate Development leadership and key stakeholders.
- Perform other duties as assigned.
Core Competencies, Skills and Experience Requirements
- Minimum of 8 or more years of professional experience, with 5 or more years of experience within the medical device, life sciences, technology, finance, investing, or related industries.
- Prior work experience in corporate development, business development, finance, investing, strategy, or another relevant discipline.
- Prior experience supporting and/or executing strategic transactions, including M&A, strategic investments, licensing, partnerships, or other business development transactions. Prior experience in corporate business development is preferred.
- Demonstrated ability to evaluate new technologies, companies, markets, and strategic opportunities and assess their potential fit with broader business and technology strategies.
- Strong business judgment, analytical capabilities, results orientation, and demonstrated interest in advancing a company's strategic position through business development activities.
- Strong financial and analytical skills, including the ability to develop business cases, financial models, valuation analyses, and market assessments.
- Ability to manage key aspects of transaction execution, including opportunity assessment, business case development, due diligence, transaction structuring, negotiations, and coordination of definitive agreements.
- Ability to coordinate cross-functional teams and work effectively with stakeholders across Strategy, Finance, Legal, R&D, Marketing, Clinical, Regulatory, and other functions as appropriate.
- Strong interpersonal and influence-management skills, with the ability to build relationships, develop alignment, and move projects forward across multiple functions and levels of the organization.
- Ability to manage significant projects and workstreams with a high degree of independence while seeking guidance and alignment on key strategic and transaction decisions.
- Strong business maturity and communication skills, with the ability to interact effectively with senior internal stakeholders and external executives, investors, entrepreneurs, and business partners.
- Analytical thinker who can synthesize complex information, identify the most important issues, and develop clear recommendations without becoming overly focused on unnecessary detail.
- Results-oriented, with the ability to take projects from initial evaluation through diligence, negotiation, and execution in collaboration with internal and external stakeholders.
- Ability to work effectively under tight deadlines and manage changing priorities while maintaining focus on key objectives.
- Excellent written, verbal, and presentation skills, with the ability to tailor communications to different audiences.
- Strong organizational and prioritization skills, with the ability to manage multiple projects and transactions simultaneously.
- Self-motivated and proactive, with a desire to contribute to the long-term strategic success of the business.
- Ability to travel, averaging 10–20% overall. Monthly travel may range from 0% to 50%.

- Bachelor's degree required, preferably with relevant experience in healthcare, medical devices, life sciences, technology, finance, or a related field.

It is also expected for this function to participate in strategic planning for the programs this position may be leading.

- Prepares justification for the programs he/she is managing, such as ROI, etc., to achieve buy in from top management.
- Plans, organizes and leads high scope projects.
- Leads and organizes project reviews affecting the Mexicali site.
- Prepares status reports for the projects and programs he/she is leading and be able to present at an executive level.
- Maintains budget control for projects and programs.
- Assures that proper documentation is prepared and updated to meet standards and regulations as required in a Medical device environment (FDA/ISO).
- Ability to influence others to perform needed tasks in order to ensure project completion on time and within budget.

jobs.title: Sr M&A Integration Manager
jobs.description:
Primary Function of Position
The Sr M&A Integration Manager reports to the Director, M&A Integrations and partners with Business Development, Finance, and functional teams to lead multiple transactions concurrently across the full deal lifecycle. The role leads cross-functional diligence planning and integration program management from pre-signing through close, Day 1, stabilization, and transition to the long-term business owner. Working with functional diligence leads, this person helps develop the integration strategy and milestones, consolidates integration costs, anticipates dependencies, drives execution, and provides clear recommendations to senior leadership.
Roles and Responsibilities
- Lead cross-functional diligence across Finance, Tax, Legal, HR, Regulatory, Quality, Sales & Marketing, Service, Product, Engineering/R&D, Operations, Supply Chain, IT, Security, and other relevant functions.
- Use the transaction rationale to build a diligence plan with clear workstreams, questions, owners, deliverables, dependencies, and decision dates.
- Establish diligence governance and cadence; ensure functional teams have the information, access, and direction needed to complete timely, decision-quality assessments.
- Coordinate management meetings, seller interactions, functional deep dives, data requests, and follow-ups with deal leaders and functional diligence leads. Prepare functional leads for seller engagement while preserving their ownership of functional conclusions.
- Guide functional leads, individually and collectively, to synthesize findings into an integrated view of risks, opportunities, cost, timing, resources, readiness, and integration complexity.
- Help functional leads develop the integration strategy, key milestones, and coordinated outputs that inform the deal model, purchase agreement, closing conditions, Day 1 requirements, integration roadmap, and long-term operating model.
- Build and maintain integrated plans spanning pre-close, close readiness, Day 1, cutover, stabilization, hypercare, longer-term integration, and transition to business ownership, with clear owners, milestones, dependencies, resources, and decisions.
- Lead integration cost estimation by coordinating functional inputs, reconciling assumptions, dependencies, and timing, and consolidating one-time and ongoing costs for deal and leadership decisions.
- Develop TSA scope, SLAs, schedules, and cost estimates based on the integration strategy and coordinated input from cross-functional teams.
- Partner with Legal to translate business, operational, and transaction requirements into purchase agreement terms and closing conditions and related deal documents.
- Partner with IT and functional teams to plan and execute systems integration, testing, data and process cutovers, access, business continuity, and hypercare; align technology milestones with business requirements.
- Coordinate with change-management and functional teams on organizational readiness, employee communications, Day 1, cutover, stabilization, and hypercare to support the employee experience.
- Lead multiple transactions concurrently at different lifecycle stages. Maintain visibility to milestones, risks, capacity, decisions, and cross-deal dependencies; recommend sequencing, resource allocation, and escalation when conflicts arise.
- Drive owners to complete deliverables and decisions and hold stakeholders accountable without formal authority.
- Manage risks, issues, assumptions, dependencies, and decisions. Identify slippage early, assess downstream effects, establish recovery plans, and escalate with a clear recommendation.
- Validate close-critical and Day 1 readiness. Transition ownership to business and functional leaders with clear accountabilities, open items, measures, and governance.
- Prepare concise, decision-oriented materials and present findings, readiness, risks, tradeoffs, options, and recommendations to executive sponsors, steering committees, and senior functional leaders.
- Build trusted relationships with sellers and acquired-company leaders while representing Intuitive requirements, protecting confidentiality, and maintaining transaction discipline.
- Support continuous improvement of Intuitive’s M&A diligence and integration playbooks, toolkit, templates, decision frameworks, governance, and operating rhythms. Convert retrospectives and lessons learned into practical improvements.
- Guide functional workstream leads and colleagues in effective diligence and integration practices. Use approved AI and productivity tools to improve planning, synthesis, reporting, and portfolio visibility while protecting confidential information.
Required Skills and Experience
- Minimum of 12 years of related experience
- Deep understanding of the M&A lifecycle, including transaction evaluation, diligence, signing, close preparation, Day 1, stabilization, post-close execution, and transition to business ownership.
- Significant experience leading cross-functional M&A diligence and integration, rather than participating solely as a functional contributor.
- Substantial experience leading buy-side M&A diligence and integrations in complex, global, or highly regulated environments.
- Proven ability to coordinate multidisciplinary teams and connect business, financial, legal, technical, operational, people, regulatory, and quality findings into an integrated point of view.
- Experience supporting transaction-structure decisions, transition service agreements, current- and future-state operating models, and value-realization tracking.
- Experience working directly with target-company leadership, executive sponsors, and senior internal stakeholders.
- Strong dependency, critical-path, and portfolio-management judgment, including prioritization across competing deals and functional capacity constraints.
- Ability to create structure in ambiguity, make progress with incomplete information, and determine when to use a standard approach, adapt it, or escalate.
- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with a record of recovering slipping plans, resolving cross-functional impasses, accelerating decisions, and driving deliverables to completion.
- Exceptional communication skills and executive presence, with the ability to drive decisions at all levels by simplifying complex issues, clarifying tradeoffs and implications, and making credible recommendations.
- Strong facilitation, negotiation, diplomacy, and influence skills; ability to align stakeholders and drive outcomes without direct authority.
- Discretion and sound judgment when handling confidential transaction information.
- Must be comfortable using approved AI tools to improve workflows across deal lifecycle and personal productivity while protecting confidential information.
- Ability to travel up to 25% domestically and internationally based on transaction needs.
- Comfort working across global time zones and cultures, with flexibility to support transaction timelines and geographically distributed stakeholders.
- This role requires working onsite in our Sunnyvale, CA office Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday every week.

Required Education and Training
- Bachelor’s degree in business, finance, engineering, operations, life sciences, or a related field, or equivalent relevant experience.

Preferred Skills and Experience
- MBA or other relevant advanced degree.
- Experience in medical technology, healthcare, life sciences, diagnostics, or another regulated technology industry.
- Cross-border transaction experience and understanding of the legal, employment, regulatory, tax, trade, quality, technology, commercial, and operational factors that shape deals
- Experience supporting software, SaaS, or technology-enabled acquisitions by enabling the back-office capabilities needed to support product teams, including cybersecurity, licensing, systems, and related operational requirements.

The Director, Finance AI and Data Governance will lead Finance-wide AI transformation by building trusted data foundations, governed semantic layers, and scalable AI capabilities that improve decision-making, productivity, controls, and business partnership. This leader will define and execute the Finance AI strategy, operating model, governance framework, and value-realization approach in close partnership with Finance leadership, Enterprise AI and Data, IT, and other enterprise partners.
The role owns Finance data governance, semantic modeling, AI agent development and design standards, use case prioritization, adoption, and measurable value delivery across financial and operational domains. This leader will establish and lead a central team of AI and data experts that shapes the future of Finance through governed, scalable, AI-driven transformation.

- Own the Finance AI and data transformation roadmap in support of the Finance team vision.

- Translate Finance strategy into a prioritized portfolio of AI and data initiatives that accelerate planning and reporting cycles, improve forecast accuracy, reduce manual work, strengthen controls, and enhance decision support.

- Establish Finance data governance policies in partnership with Enterprise AI and Data to ensure a single source of truth, high-quality data foundations, and scalable capabilities that support business needs and future growth.

- Lead governance forums that approve definitions, business rules, quality standards, lineage expectations, security, and access controls.

- Partner with functional leaders to leverage AI to improve day-to-day work, and transform business processes.

The Senior Clinical Program Manager serves as the strategic and operational partner to Clinical Development & Operations leadership, providing integrated program management across the Clinical Development & Operations portfolio from study startup through regulatory submission. The role partners with Clinical Development & Operations leadership to inform Clinical Development & Operations strategy through integrated planning, scenario analysis, governance, and execution insights, translating strategic direction into coordinated cross-functional plans that enable successful program execution.
Reporting to the Program Management & Operations organization, the Senior Clinical Program Manager partners across Clinical Development & Operations, Regulatory Affairs, Medical Affairs, CMC, Nonclinical, Quality, Commercial, and external partners to integrate timelines, risks, dependencies, and key decisions into unified program plans. In partnership with Enterprise Program Management, the role establishes Clinical Development & Operations governance and ensures cross-functional risks, dependencies, and decision requests are appropriately elevated through enterprise governance to support informed decision-making and coordinated execution.
Roles and Responsibilities
- Support the Program Management & Operations team in creating and implementing Clinical Development & Operations governance processes, including governance forums, operating cadences, decision pathways, program reporting, and the RAID framework.
- Facilitate Clinical Development & Operations & Operations governance by preparing governance materials, maintaining clinical RAID and decision logs, capturing actions and decisions, monitoring follow-through, and escalating cross-functional risks and decision requests through enterprise governance, as appropriate.

- Drive adoption of standardized project management tools, templates, dashboards, reporting practices, and workflow automation that improve portfolio visibility, consistency, and execution.

Primary Function of the Position
The Physician, Corporate Strategy is an MD physician innovator embedded within Intuitive’s Future Forward Incubator. This role translates clinical insight and early-market understanding into new growth opportunities, helping identify unmet clinical needs, evaluate strategic fit, and shape technology concepts from initial hypothesis through early de-risking. We are open to candidates who bring one of two complementary profiles: (1) strong clinical practice experience with exposure to innovation, venture, startups, business development, Biodesign, or product development; or (2) deep venture, startup, business development, Biodesign, or corporate strategy experience with an MD background and enough medical/clinical fluency to credibly assess patient care, procedure workflows, and clinician needs. The successful candidate will work closely with engineering, clinical, product, regulatory, reimbursement, and strategy partners to determine which opportunities should advance and how they should be clinically and commercially framed.

Essential Job Duties
- Identify, frame, and prioritize unmet clinical needs using clinical immersion, literature review, market sensing, and voice-of-customer input.
- Translate physician and patient insights into concise need statements, opportunity hypotheses, clinical workflows, requirements, and early de-risking plans.
- Evaluate early-stage opportunities for clinical importance, feasibility, strategic fit, adoption barriers, competitive landscape, and potential business impact.
- Partner with engineering and design teams to define clinical use cases, procedural workflows, performance goals, and prototype feedback loops for new platforms.
- Lead or support early clinical de-risking activities, including preclinical studies, simulated use, workflow validation, and early feasibility planning where appropriate.
- Develop point-of-view assessments on emerging technologies, startups, venture-backed innovation, adjacent markets, and external partnership opportunities.
- Collaborate with regulatory, reimbursement, health economics, product, and commercial strategy partners to shape indication strategy and development pathways.
- Engage KOLs, clinicians, entrepreneurs, academic innovators, and external partners to validate concepts and inform investment decisions.
- Communicate findings to senior stakeholders through clear written recommendations, executive presentations, and data-driven opportunity narratives.
